title.narrative: Leaders of Peace (Women, Peace and Security in South Sudan)

description.narrative: Beneficiaries are community members in the different locations. More specifically, women and youth as well as influential persons in the community will be targeted. Moreover, the programme will strengthen capacities and learning between consortium members and their local partners.

Result Area 1: Improved implementation of policies and regulations on GBV and protection of W/G including psychosocial support and self-care.When W/G know their rights, have access to and use MHPSS and legal protection services, while in parallel formal/ traditional authorities will implement laws and policies against GBV as well as protect survivors after being informed on these topics, W/G will be less vulnerable to physical and emotional harm .Result Area 2: Changed attitudes and beliefs of civil society to facilitate inclusion of W/G and promote gender equality.Changing harmful norms and attitudes includes transforming violent masculinities by targeting influential powerholders (men/boys) as allies and positive role models, to jointly advocate with women and youth groups for GE, as well as for equal participation of W/Y groups.Result Area 3: Increased and effective participation of W/Y in leadership and peacebuilding.Increased, influential participation of W/Y in leadership and peacebuilding is possible when W/Y facilitate political positioning and influencing across ethnic/religious/conflict lines, together with male counterparts (as well linked to RA2).The overall strategic objective of the Leaders of Peace programme is, that by the end of 2025, women and girls live in a more empowering and inclusive environment in South Sudan, where they feel safer and better enabled to realise their rights, so they can play an influential role towards conflict prevention and sustainable peace.To achieve this, the alliance will enable civil society organisations with the capacity, resources and legitimacy to influence government, and societal actors in various areas. CSOs are supported and complemented in their advocacy activities by their counterparts and/or the Ministry. At the same time, the programme mobilizes key decision makers to work towards inclusive laws, policies and norms and practices. Through lobby and advocacy of our CSO stakeholders LoP will change duty bearers’ attitude towards gender equality and female participation in decision making and the peace process.

South Sudan has been engaged in a peace process for years. It remains important to emphasize the role of women and youth in peacebuilding. The consortium consisting of Plan International, AMA (Assistance Mission for Africa), EVE, HealthNet TPO, and PAX implements the Leaders of Peace (LoP) Programme in Eastern, Western and Central Equatoria, Unity, and Lakes. Juba will be the central location to link advocacy work to national platforms and decision-makers. The LoP Alliance is led by Plan International Netherlands and is implemented in strategic partnership with the Dutch Ministry of Foreign Affairs under the Strengthening Civil Society framework (Women Peace Security grant instrument) from January 2021 to December 2025.

title.narrative: # of (female) case workers trained in age (children / adult), gender-appropriate PSS, GBV, legal protection information and are suitable to cultural context

description.narrative: Before program implementation, describe the capacity of female case workers and provide a description of the individuals, and location. In all the program locations the PFPs were new members with very limited know on protection and providing case management for GBV survivors as well as psychosocial support.

comment.narrative: In 2022, follow ups training were organised with the aim to build capacity to PFPs and case workers on lobby, facilitation and advocacy skills. The training were followed by monitoring visits and Juba programs team provided support to PFPs and case workers during the monitoring visit.

In 2023, the capacity building was aimed at improving skills of PFPs and case workers on awareness, lobbying, advocacy, peacebuilding, Gender-based Violence, Girl Child Education, early child marriages, and Human rights. Practical demonstrations took place at schools and field visit were organised to measure the effectiveness of messages delivered by the CBOs staff in specific areas as highlighted above.

What is the desired future capacity? Strengthened capacity of the community based psychosocial focal points to provide mental health and psychosocial support, GBV, case management and referrals to members of the community suffering from psychosocial consequences of GBV and mental health.

The training focuses on community mobilization skills, basic concepts mental health and psychosocial, GBV, cases management, psychosocial helping and communication skills, referral. Pre and post test tools and training evaluation tools are used to access the knowledge, attitude and skills gained. Field practicum and exercise were given out to participants as a continuous means of assessing capacity.
In 2024, refresher training were organised and were followed up visit to locations for demonstrations.

comment.narrative: What is the desired future capacity this year? Strengthened capacity of the community based psychosocial focal points to provide mental health and psychosocial support, GBV, case management and referrals to members of the community suffering from psychosocial consequences of GBV and mental health.

In 2021, the training focused on community mobilization skills, basic concepts mental health and psychosocial, GBV, cases management, psychosocial helping and communication skills, referral. Pre and post test tools and training evaluation tools were used to access the knowledge, attitude and skills gained. Field practicum and exercise were given out participants as a continuous means of assessing capacity

In 2022, HNTPO organised refresher training towards case workers. The training focuses on community mobilization skills, basic concepts mental health and psychosocial, GBV, cases management, psychosocial helping and communication skills, referral.

In 2023, there were a continuation of strengthening capacity of the community based psychosocial focal points to provide quality mental health and psychosocial support, GBV, case management and referrals to members of the community suffering from psychosocial consequences of GBV and mental health. More emphasis was put to improve the capacity of the community-based psychosocial focal points skills in psychosocial support, case management, and referrals. Not only that, they were provided more knowledge and skills on awareness creation, lobbying, and advocacy, peacebuilding, Gender-based Violence, Girl Child Education, early child marriages, and Human rights. As indicated above, Practical demonstrations in class and in the field were done to measure the effectiveness of messages delivered by the CBOs staff in specific areas of concern.

In 2024, the focus of training was on strengthening the capacity of psychosocial focal points on group approach and how they can work effectively with groups. Practical sessions were designed to help the participants practice these skills during the training session, and a field practicum was designed, and the psychosocial focal person point was supported and monitored while delivery sessions in the community. A checklist is used to monitor the expected, knowledge, skills, and attitudes of the participants. We also use pre-and post-tests to assess the knowledge gain.

title.narrative: Women-led community groups capacitated, resourced and coached on PSS, legal protection services and lobby & advocacy on these topics

comment.narrative: In 2021, the project has mobilized and trained community groups and CSO in all the project locations and engaged them to identify lobby and advocacy activities. The different community groups and CSO have demonstrated the ability to plan and implement advocacy activities. For example, CSO plans, mobilizes, and takes an active part in celebrating and calling authorities to project and respect women's rights during international events.The project developed a monitoring tool and check list that is used to measure and track progress of the CSOs

In 2022, different community groups and CSO have demonstrated ability to plan and implemented advocacy activities. For example, CSO plan, mobilized and take active part in celebration and calling authorities to project and respect women rights during international events. They have planed and carried out advocacy campaign to end child marriage and gender equality . A monitoring tool was used to measure and track progress of the CSOs. Women themselves now feel that they have space participant in public affairs. We can now air out our issues openly before men and demand for protection from duty bearers. This call made the commissioner of Terekeka County to make a public statement that his administration will ensure that women rights are respected, and perpetrators are made accountable for their actions.

In 2024, the project worked with 3 community-based groups and built their capacity to promote gender equality and raise awareness about GBV and its psychological and social impact on the individual and the community.The capacity sessions were monitored regularly through monthly and quarterly meetings. During these meetings, the performance of the group was assessed, and their capacity to engage in advocacy activities was reviewed. Based on the gaps, the team organized specific, tailored sessions for the groups to enhance their capacity. The project enabled an open discussion of issues that were previously not easily discussed. Women have gained courage and talk openly to their male counterparts and ask them to stop abusing them, marrying them and their children off at a tender age, and allowing their children, especially the girls, to go to school.

in 2023, CSOs have been instrumental in peacebuilding, Gender-based Violence, advocacy for Girl Child Education, and ending early child marriage. In collaboration with HNTPO, both CBOs played a key role in advocating for the above-mentioned thematic areas. Their popularity in the operation area (Terekeka) has improved collaboration with Civil authorities, Youth, and women in combating Violence against women and girls.The CSOs were trained and supported to implement advocacy activities in the community. This created and opened space for discussing issues of forced marriage and girls’ rights with different interlocutors.
